rule.statement: The CORRECT pole is decided by the REFERENT'S ontology, NOT by the emotional valence of the context wording. Step 1: is the referent physical/objectified or subjective-mental? Step 2 (if mental): is it objectified (treated as an external thing) or subjectified (lived as first-person experience)? Assignment: physical -> binding; mental & objectified -> binding; mental & subjectified -> liberating.
rule.note: Pole is an ontological-plane choice (gross/objectified = binding; subtle/subjective = liberating), independent of whether the emotion is 'positive' or 'negative'. So a subjectively-lived dread maps to the liberating pole under this rule even though dread is a negative emotion. This is intentional and is exactly what distinguishes this rule from B1.8's keyword-valence resolver.

anti_circularity: This classification is authored from the REFERENT ONTOLOGY only, and must be frozen and operator-approved BEFORE any generation output is produced or seen. Do not revise a row after seeing any reading. The gate refuses the real run unless classification_approved == true.

items.rationale: a rebuilt physical bridge over a river -> physical referent -> binding
a physical lantern object -> physical -> binding
an emotion lived by a subject ('in his grief he...') -> subjectified-mental -> liberating (valence NOT used)
a lived subjective emotion -> subjectified -> liberating
an abstract principle invoked/pursued as an external ideal -> objectified-mental -> binding
an abstract state treated as a thing to achieve -> objectified-mental -> binding
a physical flower as referent -> physical -> binding (BUT lotus is also a spiritual symbol; if you read it as a subjectified spiritual symbol -> liberating)
'the sacred' treated as an external quality/thing -> objectified-mental -> binding
a brand/product name (an object) -> objectified -> binding
a brand/product name (an object) -> objectified -> binding
a lived subjective emotion -> subjectified -> liberating
a lived subjective emotion -> subjectified -> liberating (valence NOT used; negative emotion still maps liberating under the rule)
